body.statement: There is a jointly measurable implementation of \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\) with the stipulated coordinate order, parent-only recursion, lexicographic child order, and separate testing of every closed child containing a shared-boundary point. For each fixed depth \(k\), its selected ambient boxes and feasible cells equal \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_j^\dagger\), respectively, for all \(j\le k\) with probability tending to one locally uniformly on every bounded nuisance fiber. Define the population prefix gaps \(\gamma_j(L)\) as in the proof and let \(j_n(L)\) be the largest certified depth for which the approximation envelope is smaller than all preceding positive prefix gaps. Then \(a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0\) and \(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P(a_n(L))\) locally uniformly. This conclusion includes disconnected, flat, tied, and dyadic-boundary minimizing sets. A jointly refined rectangle-constant Gaussian rule has risk error \(o(1)\) uniformly over every fixed bounded nuisance fiber. The final rate limitation is only a generic continuous-objective statement: on \([0,1]\), continuity and uniform objective-approximation control alone imply no spatial recovery modulus tending to zero uniformly over all continuous objectives, because for every \(\epsilon>0\), \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\) have canonical minimizers zero and one while \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\) is within \(\epsilon/2\) uniformly of both. No model-specific impossibility over the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\) is asserted.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and write \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\).  The stipulated spaces of \(p\) and \(e\) imply \(c_{ax}>0\) in each of the finitely many cells.  Because \(L\ge2\) and the support values are distinct, choose \(y_u\ne y_w\).  For any probability vector \(q_{ax}\), expansion around its mean gives
\[
 \sigma^2_{ax}(q)=\sum_{\ell<m}q_{ax\ell}q_{axm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2.
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta\) by \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\),
\[
 \underline\sigma^2:=\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2
 \le\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)\le4C_Y^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus two support points, and not a third, are sufficient for the positive variance floor.

For \(z\in\mathbb R^d\), the covariance definition gives
\[
 z^\top\Sigma(r)z
 =\sum_{x=1}^K\sum_{a=0}^1
   \frac{p_x\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}(z^\top d_x)^2.
\tag{13}
\]
The coefficients in (13) have fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds because \(r_{ax}\in[\rho,1]\), \(p_x,e_{ax}>0\), and (12) holds.  Moreover \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\), and \(F=[d_1\;\cdots\;d_K]\operatorname{diag}(p)\) with positive diagonal \(\operatorname{diag}(p)\), so \(d_1,\ldots,d_K\) span \(\mathbb R^d\).  Hence \(z\mapsto\sum_x(z^\top d_x)^2\) has a positive minimum on the unit sphere.  Equation (13) places
\[
 \{\Sigma(r):r\in\mathcal R_B\}
\quad\text{in a fixed compact set}\quad
 \mathcal K\subset\mathbb S_{++}^d.
\tag{14}
\]

We next build a uniformly accurate pilot objective under the two stipulated pilot limits.  Put
\[
 b_n=m_n^{-1/4}+n^{-1/2},
 \qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
The assumption \(m_n\to\infty\) gives \(b_n\to0\), \(t_n\to0\), and
\[
 b_n/t_n=b_n^{1/2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Let \(N_{ax}\) count fully labelled pilot records in cell \((a,x)\).  For \(s\in\{1,2\}\), let \(\widehat\nu_{s,ax}\) be the within-cell mean of \(Y^s\), with any value in the bounded range when \(N_{ax}=0\), and write
\(\nu_{s,ax,n}=E_{q_n(h,v)}(Y^s\mid A=a,X=x)\).  Uniformly in \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\), boundedness of \(Y\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac{N_{ax}}{m_n}\right)
 \le\frac{c_{ax}}{m_n},
 \qquad
 E\!\left[
 \left\{\frac1{m_n}\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}
 \mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}(Y_i^s-\nu_{s,ax,n})\right\}^2
 \right]
 \le\frac{c_{ax}(2C_Y^s)^2}{m_n}.
\tag{17}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality first yields
\(P(N_{ax}<m_nc_{ax}/2)=O(m_n^{-1})\).  On the complementary event, division by \(N_{ax}/m_n\ge c_{ax}/2\) in the second display in (17), followed again by Chebyshev at threshold \(m_n^{-1/4}\), yields constants \(C_{ax,s}\) such that
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\!left(
 |\widehat\nu_{s,ax}-\nu_{s,ax,n}|>C_{ax,s}m_n^{-1/4}
 \right)=O(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{18}
\]
The constants are uniform because only the fixed cell probabilities and the bound on \(Y\) enter.  A union bound over the fixed \(4K\) coordinates supplies events \(E_n(C_v)\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 P_{q_n(h,v)}\{E_n(C_v)\}\longrightarrow1.
\tag{19}
\]

Continuity of \((h,v)\mapsto S_0h+Wv\) on the compact bounded-fiber domain gives a finite uniform bound on \(\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty\).  Since \(q_n-q^0=s(h,v)/\sqrt n\) and the support is finite,
\[
 \max_{a,x,\,s\in\{1,2\}}
 |\nu_{s,ax,n}-\nu_{s,ax,0}|\le C(C_v)n^{-1/2}.
\tag{20}
\]
The map \((\nu_1,\nu_2)\mapsto\nu_2-\nu_1^2\) is Lipschitz on the bounded moment rectangle.  Clip the resulting pilot variance estimates to \([\underline\sigma^2/2,4C_Y^2]\).  Equations (18)--(20) imply on \(E_n(C_v)\)
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\widehat\sigma^2_{ax}-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|
 \le C_0(C_v)b_n.
\tag{21}
\]
No comparison between \(m_n\) and \(\sqrt n\) was used.

Let \(\widehat\Sigma_n(r)\) replace the cell variances in \(\Sigma(r)\) by the clipped pilot estimates, and let \(\widehat L_n(r)\) be the corresponding Gaussian minimax value.  Since \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), (21) gives
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}
 \lVert\widehat\Sigma_n(r)-\Sigma(r)\rVert
 \le C_1(C_v)b_n.
\tag{22}
\]
For positive-definite matrices \(S,S'\) in a sufficiently small compact enlargement of \(\mathcal K\), set \(S_t=(1-t)S+tS'\).  Differentiation of the centered normal density gives
\[
 \frac{d}{dt}\phi_{S_t}(z)
 =\frac12\phi_{S_t}(z)
 \left[z^\top S_t^{-1}(S'-S)S_t^{-1}z
       -\operatorname{tr}\{S_t^{-1}(S'-S)\}\right].
\tag{23}
\]
The common eigenvalue bounds from (14), integration in \(z\) and \(t\), and translation invariance imply
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^d}
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h,S')\}
 \le C_2\lVert S-S'\rVert.
\tag{24}
\]
The regret is bounded by
\(R_H=2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty<\infty\).  Thus changing \(S\) to \(S'\) changes the risk of every rule at every state by at most \(R_H\) times (24).  Taking successively the supremum over states and the infimum over rules, in both directions, yields from (22)
\[
 \sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}|\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)|
 \le C_3(C_v)b_n
 \quad\text{on }E_n(C_v).
\tag{25}
\]

We now construct the nested-cell selector.  Set
\(k_n=\max\{0,\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\rfloor\}\).  Through depth \(k_n\), use precisely the coordinate order, parent-only recursion, closed-child convention, and lexicographic order in \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\).  On every nonempty feasible part of a child of the currently selected parent, approximate the minimum of \(\widehat L_n\) with deterministic error at most \(b_n\).

Such finite approximations exist uniformly.  Indeed, \(P_B\) is continuous and equals the identity on \(\mathcal R_B\), so projecting refining ambient finite nets through \(P_B\) gives dense finite nets in \(\mathcal R_B\).  If \(C=\mathcal R_B\cap D\) is a nonempty closed child cell, project each such point \(g\) onto the compact convex set \(C\).  The nearest point \(c_C(g)\) exists and is unique; if \(c\in C\) and \(\lVert g-c\rVert\le\xi\), then
\[
 \lVert c_C(g)-c\rVert
 \le\lVert c_C(g)-g\rVert+\lVert g-c\rVert\le2\xi.
\tag{26}
\]
Thus the cellwise nets refine even for singleton cells and cells contained in a dyadic boundary.  On represented inputs, \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), after adding the child's rational box inequalities, supplies terminating outward certificates.  For a fixed mathematical instance, deterministic simple-function refinement gives the same approximation without an effectiveness assertion.

For completeness, the Gaussian-game approximation is uniform.  Differentiating a Gaussian density in its mean as in (23) gives, uniformly for \(S\in\mathcal K\),
\[
 \operatorname{TV}\{N(h,S),N(h',S)\}\le C_5\lVert h-h'\rVert.
\tag{27}
\]
The loss is uniformly Lipschitz in \(h\), so every rule's risk has a common modulus on compact \(\mathcal H\).  A finite state net therefore approximates all worst-state risks uniformly.  For finite state and covariance nets, let \(\mu\) be the sum of the finitely many Gaussian laws.  Rational rectangles generate the Borel sigma-field; consequently every measurable simplex-valued rule admits rectangle-simple component approximations in \(L^1(\mu)\).  Projection of their values onto \(\Delta_M\) preserves measurability and convergence.  A covariance net and (24) make the approximation uniform over \(\mathcal K\).  Taking a rule arbitrarily close to the defining infimum proves convergence of the finite rectangle games to the Gaussian games.  All finite-stage operations are Borel functions of the pilot moments, and lexicographic resolution of finitely many comparisons makes the design selector jointly measurable.

Let \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\) denote the approximate value of feasible child \(b\) at depth \(j\).  When the parent is the population box \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), put
\[
 v_{j,b}=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B\cap D_{j,b}}L(r).
\]
Combining (25) with the numerical tolerance gives a deterministic
\(\alpha_n=C_4(C_v)b_n\) such that, on \(E_n(C_v)\),
\[
 |\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}|\le\alpha_n
\tag{28}
\]
simultaneously for all children tested through depth \(k_n\).  By (16), \(\alpha_n=o(t_n)\).  Retain exactly the siblings satisfying
\[
 \widehat v_{n,j,b}\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\tag{29}
\]
and choose the lexicographically first retained child.  The sibling attaining the finite approximate minimum is retained, so the empirical cell is nonempty; parent-only recursion makes the empirical cells nested.

For the feasible children of \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), define
\[
 E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_j(L)=
 \begin{cases}
 \min_{b\notin E_j}(v_{j,b}-V^*),&
 E_j\text{ is not all feasible children},\\
 +\infty,&E_j\text{ is all feasible children}.
 \end{cases}
\tag{30}
\]
At least one child belongs to \(E_j\), because the finitely many closed children cover the selected compact parent cell, which contains a minimizer.  Continuity of \(L\), itself a consequence of the covariance formula and (24), makes every child minimum attained.  Hence every child outside \(E_j\) has value strictly larger than \(V^*\), and finiteness gives \(\gamma_j(L)>0\).

Assume inductively that the empirical parent at depth \(j-1\) equals \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  Under (28), every child in \(E_j\) is retained whenever \(2\alpha_n<t_n\), while every child outside \(E_j\) is rejected whenever
\[
 t_n+2\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L).
\tag{31}
\]
Under these inequalities the retained children are exactly \(E_j\), and their lexicographically first member is \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\).  Induction proves stabilization of every fixed prefix.  If a minimizer lies on a shared dyadic boundary, every closed child containing it is separately feasible and lies in \(E_j\); all are retained before the same lexicographic rule is applied.  Disconnected, flat, or separated tied minimizing sets only enlarge \(E_j\).  Thus (28)--(31) cover both separated ties and dyadic-boundary minima.

The outward cell bounds from \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\), or deterministic convergent bounds for a fixed instance, eventually certify a positive lower bound for each finite positive gap in (30).  Let \(j_n(L)\le k_n\) be the largest certified depth for which the approximation envelope is smaller than all positive prefix gaps through that depth, with \(j_n(L)=0\) if there is no such level.  This is an analysis sequence depending on the pilot schedule and the population prefix-separation profile, not on \(C_v\).  For every fixed depth, (16), (28), and positivity of the finitely many preceding gaps eventually imply (31).  Since \(k_n\to\infty\),
\[
 j_n(L)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 a_n(L):=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}\downarrow0.
\tag{32}
\]
Choose a point from the final selected compact feasible cell by successively minimizing its coordinates; this fixed rule is Borel measurable on the countable family of cells.  On \(E_n(C_v)\), both that point \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) belong to the same depth-\(j_n(L)\) population cell.  The dyadic diameter bound gives
\[
 \lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
 \le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L).
\tag{33}
\]
Equations (19), (32), and (33) establish local uniform convergence in probability and
\(\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P\{a_n(L)\}\).  The rate is necessarily schedule- and law-specific through (15) and the gaps (30).

It remains to couple the selector to the terminal Gaussian rule.  At deterministic refinement level \(s\), use \(\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\), a finite state net, and a rational observation-rectangle partition after tail truncation, and solve the finite Gaussian game to total error at most \(2^{-s}\), resolving finite ties lexicographically.  Let \(J_s<\infty\) be the number of rectangles.  A diagonal choice \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) can be made slowly enough that
\[
 J_{s_n}n^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{34}
\]
while the state-mesh, tail, quadrature, rounding, covariance, and finite-game errors vanish.  Each level uses only finitely many Borel pilot statistics and comparisons, so the rectangle rule is jointly measurable with \(\widehat r_n\).

To verify its distributional coupling, put \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), \(b=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\), and, conditionally on \(\mathscr P_n\), define
\[
 H_{i,ax}=
 \frac{\mathbf1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 (Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{35}
\]
Annotation ignorability gives \(E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=b\).  The conditional summands \(A_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)\) are centered and uniformly bounded because \(Y\) and the clipped pilot means are bounded, \(p_xe_{ax}>0\), and \(\widehat r_{n,ax}\ge\rho\).  Only one coordinate of \(H_i\) can be nonzero, so their exact conditional covariance is
\[
 S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)+b_{ax}^2}
 {p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
 \right\}-bb^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{36}
\]
The bracketed \(b\)-remainder is itself a covariance matrix and is positive semidefinite.  The same bounded-cell second-moment argument as in (17) gives, locally uniformly,
\[
 \lVert b\rVert=O_P(m_n^{-1/2}).
\tag{37}
\]
The affine local chart gives
\[
 \max_{a,x}|\sigma^2_{ax}(q_n)-\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)|=O(n^{-1/2})
\tag{38}
\]
uniformly on the bounded fiber.  The \((0,x)\) and \((1,x)\) columns of \(A_{\mathrm{map}}\) are \(-p_xd_x\) and \(p_xd_x\), respectively, and therefore
\[
 A_{\mathrm{map}}\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
 \frac{\sigma^2_{ax}(q^0)}{p_xe_{ax}r_{ax}}
 \right\}A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top=\Sigma(r).
\tag{39}
\]
Equations (33), (36)--(39), and continuity of reciprocal rates on \([\rho,1]\) imply
\[
 \lVert S_n-\Sigma(r^\dagger)\rVert
 =O_P\{m_n^{-1}+n^{-1/2}+a_n(L)\}=o_P(1)
\tag{40}
\]
locally uniformly.  This covariance step needs only \(m_n\to\infty\).

By (12)--(14), (38), and (40), \(S_n\) has a common positive lower eigenvalue with probability tending to one uniformly on the bounded fiber.  Normalize the \(n\) summands in the exact identity
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-b)
\tag{41}
\]
by \(S_n^{-1/2}\).  Uniform boundedness makes the sum of the third absolute Euclidean moments of the normalized scaled summands \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The frozen \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) therefore bounds the conditional probability error of every observation rectangle by \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  Summing over the \(J_{s_n}\) rectangles and using (34), then applying (24) and (40), yields
\[
 \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
 |\operatorname{Risk}_n(h,v)-\operatorname{Risk}_{G,n}(h,v)|=o(1).
\tag{42}
\]
The Gaussian comparison has mean \(h\), as given by the local mean identity in the established \(\mathrm{thm:nuisance\text{-}uniform\text{-}experiment}\), and covariance \(\Sigma(r^\dagger)\).  Bounded regret turns the locally uniform conditional convergence in probability into unconditional convergence.  The separate condition \(m_n/n\to0\) in \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\) makes the pilot likelihood negligible in that established experiment theorem.  This proves the claimed jointly refined Gaussian-rule risk coupling for every \(L\ge2\).

Finally, the rate limitation is purely generic.  For \(\epsilon>0\), define on \([0,1]\)
\[
 f_+(z)=\epsilon z,
 \qquad f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z),
 \qquad g(z)=\epsilon/2.
\tag{43}
\]
The canonical minimizers of \(f_+\) and \(f_-\) are zero and one, whereas
\[
 \lVert g-f_+\rVert_\infty=\lVert g-f_-\rVert_\infty=\epsilon/2.
\tag{44}
\]
Any selector seeing the common approximation \(g\) returns the same \(z_g\) in both cases, and
\[
 \max\{|z_g|,|z_g-1|\}\ge\tfrac12.
\tag{45}
\]
Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) rules out a spatial recovery modulus uniform over all continuous objectives when only continuity and uniform objective error are controlled.  Since (43) is not claimed to belong to the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\), no model-specific impossibility is asserted.
body.justification: For every known fixed finite support with \(L\ge2\), two distinct values give the variance floor needed by the jointly measurable deterministic-limit selector. The construction works from any diverging, vanishing-share pilot, stabilizes every fixed nested-cell prefix at nonunique and boundary optima, supplies a schedule- and law-specific spatial rate, and couples the selector to a slowly refining Gaussian rectangle rule.
body.gap: The selector rate depends jointly on the pilot schedule and the objective's certified prefix-separation profile. The proof's counterexample establishes only that generic continuity plus uniform objective-approximation control cannot yield an objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus; it makes no model-specific impossibility claim for the Gaussian-risk family.
body.consumer: This theorem supplies the implementable design and decision schedule required by the full-nuisance attainment theorem, even when the fully labelled pilot diverges arbitrarily slowly.
